The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[-3,7],$ is shown above. It consists of line segments.

Find the average value ${f}_{\text{avg}}$ of $f(x)$ on $[-2,6].$ Do not round the answer.

worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is 

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-2,2].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have 

$$
{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x={A}_{1}=2.
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [2,6].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 4\cdot 2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{2}=-4.
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}-{A}_{2} \\  & =2-4 \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6-(-2)}\cdot (-2) \\  & =-\frac{2}{8} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
